newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-FEARLESS HINGIS LOOKS FORWARD TO GRAF MATCH IN FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-FEARLESS HINGIS LOOKS FORWARD TO GRAF MATCH IN FINAL.

text.p: Bring on Steffi Graf, make it best-of-five sets and put $500,000 on the table for the winner -- you still won't rattle fearless young Martina Hingis.

The 16-year-old Swiss player beat friend and former doubles partner Iva Majoli 6-2 4-6 6-1 in the semifinals of the 16-player Chase Championships to reach Sunday's final against world number one Graf.
"It's a great feeling," Hingis said about making the final in her first try at the season-ending championships. "I've had a great last few weeks and I played just great tennis."

Hingis has already had a busy season against Graf -- she beat her in the quarters of the Italian Open last May, lost to the German in the fourth round at Wimbledon and held a set point before losing to Graf in the U.S. Open semifinals.
"I had a great match against her at the U.S. Open, and I had four set points in the first set," the cheerful teenager said. "I will try to do it tomorrow better and just take every point I can get."
Graf advanced to the old guard/new wave final with a 4-6 6-4 6-3 victory over Jana Novotna.

The hard-hitting Hingis, who has shot up the rankings to number five after winning two weeks ago at Oakland where she trounced Monica Seles in the final, is not fazed about playing her first best-of-five match on Sunday.

"I've never had big problems about being long on the court," she said. "During the U.S. Open I played three events (singles, doubles, mixed doubles) and some people asked me if I want to stay overnight on the court."
The vivacious Hingis showed she had enough energy to go around, reaching the semifinals of each event.

Hingis singled out her doubles triumph with partner Helena Sukova at Wimbledon -- where she became the youngest champion ever crowned at the All-England Club championships -- as the turning point of her season.

"The Wimbledon doubles final, even if it was only doubles, gave me much more confidence," Hingis said. "And then I practiced a lot before the U.S. Open and I took it over to the singles and I made a semifinals there.
"And then finally I won my first event in Germany, in Filderstadt, and it was a big help to me me. I knew I can be a winner in a big tournament."
Asked if being called the likely successor to Graf has put any extra pressure on her, Hingis replied: "It doesn't make me nervous at all. I just try to play my best tennis against her tomorrow.
"I won two tournaments, I make semis and finals. So I think right now I'm where I should be. But you never know, it's a long, hard way to get to be number one."
